title: Why You Shouldn't Reward Students For Good Behavior
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes the case against using extrinsic rewards - stickers, pizza parties, extra recess - to incentivize good behavior in general education classrooms. He outlines four specific harms: rewards reframe good behavior as effortful "work," create a sense of entitlement to compensation for baseline expectations, cheapen the intrinsic value of being a respected class member, and require ever-escalating payouts to maintain their effect over time. In place of rewards, he advocates building a classroom that students genuinely enjoy being part of, so that belonging and self-respect become the motivating forces instead of external prizes. The article positions intrinsic motivation as both more sustainable and more meaningful than any incentive system.
points: Rewards reframe good behavior as effortful "work" that must be paid for.
Reward systems create entitlement, teaching students they are owed something for baseline expected behavior.
Extrinsic rewards cheapen the intrinsic value of belonging to and contributing to the class.
Reward systems require escalating frequency and value over time to remain effective.
A classroom students love being part of is framed as the most powerful and sustainable reward available.
quotes: For regular education classroom teachers, giving rewards in exchange for good behavior is a mistake.
Rewarding good behavior sends the message to your students that if they have to be paid for it, then it must be work.
When you offer rewards in return for good behavior, you create in your students a peculiar sense of entitlement. They’ll feel entitled to receive something for merely doing what is expected.
Being rewarded to behave cheapens the intrinsic merit of being a valued citizen of your class. In other words, it puts a price tag on the priceless.
When you put a price tag on good behavior by offering rewards, your students will demand higher and more frequent payments.
Good behavior is its own reward because it offers students self-respect, confidence, and the wonderful feeling of belonging to a classroom that needs and appreciates them.
Stop interfering with the awesome power of intrinsic motivation.
